chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from more than one, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

A man who accepts in exchange the jizyah (poll tax) of men's heads, and the kharaj (land tax) of date palms, al-ajam (likely dates or a specific crop), and birds, while he does not know whether any of these will ever materialize or not. He (the Imam) said: 'If he knows of one thing that has come into existence, then buy it and accept it from him.'

key_terms.الآجام: A specific type of crop or produce (often dates)
key_terms.الغرر: Uncertainty or ambiguity in contract terms

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling uncertain or contingent assets in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *gharar* (uncertainty) in trade, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a sale of contingent assets is valid if the seller possesses knowledge of at least one existing item to anchor the contract, thereby mitigating total ambiguity. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that partial knowledge of existence suffices to validate the transaction, distinguishing it from pure speculation where no underlying asset is known to exist.
